column4: Validate provider webhook signatures before admitting work
column5: Tampered body, wrong URL and invalid signature each create no case or action; valid vendor fixtures pass.

column4: Persist and deduplicate incoming events by tenant, provider and external event identity
column5: Replaying one event 20 times yields one case effect; same identifier in another tenant stays independent.

column4: Keep a durable case independent of temporary routing resources
column5: Expired/deleted task still leaves full case history, owner and unresolved customer request visible.

column4: Verify customer identity before revealing account-specific information
column5: Unverified sender gets generic help; mismatched account cannot retrieve another customer order.

column4: Enforce tenant and record permissions across retrieval, tools and exports
column5: Adversarial cross-tenant identifiers and disallowed knowledge return denial without data exposure.

column4: Set public/private visibility explicitly on every comment action
column5: Internal-note content never appears in customer reply, retrieval context for that customer or exported transcript.

column4: Preserve actor, displayed author and authenticated updater separately
column5: Audit readback distinguishes the service account from the employee shown as author.

column4: Check reply size and attachment destination before sending
column5: Oversized body is held for editing; external attachment fetch sends no vendor credentials and obeys size/type limits.

column4: Use approved versioned knowledge with owner, access scope and expiry
column5: Expired or inaccessible article is excluded; an answer records the article version supporting it.

column4: Escalate unsupported answers and hostile instructions in customer content
column5: A request to ignore policy cannot expand tool authority; absent evidence yields a handoff rather than invented policy.

column4: Model queue, routing task and reservation as separate linked records
column5: Rejected reservation remains in history and a new offer links to the same unresolved case.

column4: Confirm acceptance before treating a human handoff as complete
column5: Timeout/no available worker leaves a named queue owner and fallback callback task; customer sees an accurate pending state.

column4: Fence automated replies as soon as human takeover is committed
column5: Concurrent queued bot send and takeover permit no bot send after the takeover version commits.

column4: Re-read and resolve version conflicts before changing task state
column5: Stale If-Match gets 412; newer owner/state survives and operator receives the conflict.

column4: Configure skills, capacity, business hours, overflow and abandonment rules
column5: After-hours, full-capacity and abandoned-request scenarios preserve a recoverable case and correct destination.

column4: Persist outbound intent and use an idempotent dispatch boundary
column5: Crash before send, during send and after acknowledgment is recovered without claiming unconfirmed delivery.

column4: Represent ambiguous provider outcomes explicitly and reconcile them
column5: A send timeout records outcome unknown; readback or human resolution establishes its result before retry.

column4: Keep money-moving actions outside the first pilot; design their approval contract
column5: Refund request captures order, amount, currency and responsible owner, but cannot execute a refund in pilot.

column4: Scope future payment idempotency to provider API version and operation identity
column5: For an approved future refund, changed parameters cannot reuse a key; pruned-key and repeated-500 recovery uses authoritative lookup.

column4: Reconcile missed events using provider-supported read APIs and checkpoints
column5: A deliberately omitted webhook is recovered from a known fixture; checkpoint advances only after durable application.

column4: Bound retries, record dead letters and provide an operator recovery queue
column5: Persistent provider failure ends in visible manual recovery with attempt history, without silently dropping the case.

column4: Treat multi-request task completion as a recoverable workflow
column5: Failure between attribute update and completion does not mark the case resolved; recovery reads both outcomes.

column4: Use managed secret references, least privilege and rotation
column5: Revoked integration credential stops actions visibly; replacement succeeds without credentials in receipts or exports.

column4: Record append-only action history with retention and redacted logs
column5: Case owner can reconstruct each action and decision; retention deletion removes scoped content with an auditable receipt.

column4: Define SLA clocks, pause reasons, timezone and escalation owner
column5: Weekend, daylight-saving and waiting-on-customer fixtures match the signed service schedule.

column4: Measure successful resolution separately from bot response or handoff
column5: Dashboard reports eligible cases, repeat contacts, acceptance failures, confirmed delivery and correction rate with clear denominators.

column4: Provide kill switch, export, restore and vendor outage runbook
column5: Operator disables automated sends, restores a fixture backup and resumes only after reconciliation.

column4: Gate pilot on evaluated cases and actual sandbox workflows
column5: Signed pilot corpus includes happy path, ambiguity, wrong identity, stale policy, duplicate, omission, timeout, race and unavailable human; no unexplained high-risk failures.

column4: Sign scope, authoritative systems, dependencies and support ownership
column5: Client approves included intents/channels, integration access, exceptions, data handling and exit deliverables before go-live.

column4: Establish baseline volumes and a costed pilot budget
column5: Client inputs measured eligible volume, handling time, provider usage and QA/support effort; budget states uncertainty and stop threshold.

column4: Scope voice, recording, telecom and jurisdiction obligations separately
column5: Before voice launch, responsible owner records applicable consent, recording, number/channel provisioning and specialist decisions for each served location.

column4: Assess assurance and sector obligations against actual customer requirements
column5: Procurement/data classification review identifies requested attestations, contractual controls and any specialist signoff; no certification is inferred from vendor selection.
